metaTitle: Stucco Repair in Cochrane & Okotoks | Sandstone Stucco Co
metaDescription: Stucco repair in Cochrane and Okotoks: hail, flicker holes, cracks and parging quoted by independent contractors. No-obligation quotes. Call (403) 555-0148.
heroSub: Two foothills towns west and south of Calgary, both of which grew between the 2016 and 2021 censuses. Tell us what your wall looks like and an independent stucco contractor quotes the job after seeing it.
introHtml:
Stucco repair in Cochrane and Okotoks starts the same way it does in Calgary: someone walks the wall, finds where the finish has cracked, pocked or lost its bond, and writes down what the fix involves. Sandstone Stucco Co is an advertising service, paid by contractors, that puts homeowners in touch with independent stucco contractors. We do not do the work ourselves, and the contractor who quotes your job contracts directly with you.

Both towns have grown, Cochrane much faster. Cochrane had 32,199 people in 2021, up 24.5% from 2016, in 12,578 private dwellings, and Okotoks had 30,405, up 4.8%, in 10,750 dwellings (2021 census).

services.title: Hail damage scope
services.desc: Pocked or cracked stucco after a storm can be walked by a contractor who writes up a repair estimate. You can give that written estimate to your insurer; the claim itself stays between you and your insurer.

services.title: Flicker and woodpecker holes
services.desc: Northern flickers are federally protected, so a hole has to be empty before anyone touches it. A contractor can then patch it and talk through non-harmful deterrents such as mesh.

services.title: Cracks, bulges and window trim
services.desc: Cracks at corners, around windows or at the base of a wall can let water in before you see a stain. A contractor can look at where moisture may be getting behind the finish and quote the repair.

services.title: Foundation parging and recoats
services.desc: Flaking or crumbling parging on the visible part of the foundation, and tired or patchy finish coats, can be quoted for repair or recoating. Cracks in the foundation wall itself are a separate question for a structural specialist.

sections.heading: Hail in the foothills: what is on record and what is not
sections.html:
Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) reported that in 2024 two storms formed "along the southern Alberta foothills", and the southern one dropped baseball-sized hail on rural lands southeast of Calgary. That is the closest foothills reference we can point to. No primary source we have read names a specific hail event in Cochrane or Okotoks, so we will not describe one.

The City of Calgary says all communities within Calgary are equally exposed to hail, and that Calgary sits in what it calls hail alley. That statement is about Calgary, not these towns. The only way to know about your own wall is to have someone look at it.

The Insurance Bureau of Canada (IBC) says hail damage is typically covered by home insurance policies, and it advises documenting damage with photos and calling your insurer or its claims department to report it. Check your own policy, and read our hail and woodpecker damage guide for the wider picture. A contractor can supply a written repair estimate; we do not file, negotiate or manage claims.

sections.heading: Newer homes, older homes, and what that means for the wall
sections.html:
Cochrane grew by 24.5% between 2016 and 2021. A newer home may still be inside its new home warranty: Alberta's New Home Buyer Protection Act requires at least five years of building-envelope defect coverage on homes built under a permit applied for on or after 1 February 2014. Hail damage is not a defect, but a wall that is cracking early for no clear reason is worth checking against your warranty before you pay anyone.

Okotoks grew more slowly, 4.8% since 2016, and we have no dwelling-age breakdown for either town, so we will not guess at how old your stucco is. Calgary's own figures show how varied a housing stock can be: 26% of its occupied dwellings were built 1961-1980 and 20% were built 2001-2010. Whether your wall has a cement or an acrylic finish changes how a repair is done and how well a patch matches.

If you are buying a stucco house in either town, our stucco repair overview is a place to start. Before you sign, consider having the wall looked at by a stucco contractor or a building-envelope inspector.

sections.heading: Weather, timing and permits
sections.html:
The freeze-thaw and chinook data we have is for Calgary: 117 freeze-thaw cycles in 2022, below the 30-year average of 128, and 54 chinook days against an average of 46. We have no separate count for Cochrane or Okotoks. Martini Stone Masonry, a Calgary contractor, describes water getting into small cracks, freezing and expanding, and the City of Calgary notes that moisture and snow can cause stucco to shrink and crack.

Stucco needs mild, dry weather to cure. Manufacturer guidance we have read sets a minimum of about 4 to 5°C at the wall, so many exterior repairs wait for spring. A contractor can still look at the wall in winter and tell you what can wait; see what stucco repair costs for how firms publish their prices.

On permits, the City of Calgary says most like-for-like repair or replacement work does not need a permit, while changing to a different cladding material does. Those are Calgary's rules, and they are the ones we have read. Cochrane and Okotoks each set their own, so confirm with your town before you start and ask any contractor to name the licences they hold.

faq.q: Which parts of Cochrane and Okotoks do the contractors cover?
faq.a: Sandstone Stucco Co advertises independent stucco contractors across Calgary, Airdrie, Chestermere, Cochrane and Okotoks. Which contractor takes your job, and when they can visit, depends on their own schedule. Call (403) 555-0148 or send the form and describe the wall.

faq.q: Did a hailstorm hit Cochrane or Okotoks?
faq.a: We have not found a primary source that names hail in either town, so we do not claim one. ECCC did report that two 2024 storms formed along the southern Alberta foothills, and that the southern one dropped baseball-sized hail on rural land southeast of Calgary. If your wall is marked, document it with photos and report it to your insurer.

faq.q: A flicker has drilled holes in my wall. Can I fill them myself?
faq.a: Northern flickers are federally protected, so do not harm the bird or disturb a hole with eggs or chicks in it. ECCC says covering an area with a tarp or wire mesh is allowed if it does not harm the bird. Once nesting is finished, a contractor can patch the empty holes.

faq.q: Do I need a permit to repair stucco in Cochrane or Okotoks?
faq.a: The City of Calgary says most repairs done with the same material do not need a building permit, but changing to a different cladding does. Cochrane and Okotoks set their own permit rules, and we have not read them. Ask your town office before work starts.
